prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to point you to the single “best” broker I need a bit more about your situation. Quick questions:

- Are you buying just for yourself or for a family?  
- Do you want a plan on the ACA marketplace (to get premium tax credits) or off‑exchange/short‑term/Medicare?  
- Any regular prescriptions or ongoing specialist care?  
- What ZIP code in Kansas City (MO) are you in?

While you answer, here’s how to find the best broker for a self‑employed person and what to ask them.

How to choose a broker (what matters for self‑employed people)
- Looks at both on‑exchange (ACA) and off‑exchange plans, so you get subsidy-eligible options.  
- Independent agent/broker (not captive to one insurer) so they can compare multiple carriers.  
- Experience enrolling self‑employed clients and understanding how fluctuating income affects subsidies.  
- Can advise on HSAs, catastrophic plans, and when short‑term or level‑funded options make sense.  
- Good reviews or referrals and clear fee disclosure (most individual enrollments fee-free because carriers pay commissions).

Where to search and compare
- HealthCare.gov local help finder for in‑person assister/Navigator help: https://localhelp.healthcare.gov/  
- HealthSherpa — simple ACA marketplace shopping and enrollment: https://www.healthsherpa.com/  
- eHealth — aggregates individual/off‑exchange plan options: https://www.ehealthinsurance.com/  
- NAHU “Find an Agent” (National Association of Health Underwriters): https://www.nahu.org/  
- Missouri Insurance licensing/agent lookup (verify a broker is licensed): https://insurance.mo.gov/consumers/Agents/agentsearch.php

Questions to ask any broker/agent
1. Are you an independent agent? Which carriers do you work with?  
2. Do you help enroll on the ACA marketplace and with subsidy calculations?  
3. How do you get paid and are there any client fees?  
4. How many self‑employed/sole proprietor clients have you helped?  
5. Will you help with end‑of‑year income adjustments if my earnings change?  
6. What’s the expected turnaround/timeframe to enroll?  
7. Can you explain the differences between plan types (HMO/PPO, HSA‑eligible, catastrophic)?  
8. Do you provide ongoing support (claims/denials) after enrollment?

Red flags
- Pushes only one carrier or refuses to show comparisons.  
- Wants a client fee in addition to standard commissions (not necessarily bad, but get a clear reason).  
- Unable to explain how subsidies work or how changing income affects premium tax credits.

If you give your ZIP code and preferences (ACA vs off‑exchange, budget, Rx needs), I’ll find and recommend 2–3 well‑rated independent brokers or assister options in Kansas City, MO and summarize reviews and whether they handle ACA subsidies for self‑employed clients.
